---
name: Implementation experience or pilot evidence
about: Share structured evidence from applying SDAF or a defined subset
title: "[Pilot evidence] "
labels: ""
assignees: ""
---

## SDAF version

Identify the SDAF version used, for example `1.0`.

## Implementation status

Select the most accurate description:

- [ ] Planned pilot
- [ ] Pilot in progress
- [ ] Completed pilot
- [ ] Operational implementation
- [ ] Retrospective assessment
- [ ] Partial or adapted application

## Context and objective

Describe the decision, system or problem being addressed and the intended value of applying SDAF.

## Scope and boundaries

Describe:

- system or service boundary;
- organizational boundary;
- lifecycle stages included;
- assessment period;
- geographic scope; and
- material exclusions.

## SDAF coverage

Identify the Parts, phases, requirements, annexes and templates applied.

If only a subset was used, explain how that subset was selected.

## Participants and capability

Describe the relevant participant roles and their prior familiarity with:

- sustainability;
- lifecycle assessment;
- architecture;
- measurement;
- governance; and
- assurance.

Do not identify individuals without permission.

## Evidence and methods

Describe:

- evidence sources;
- measurement methods;
- functional unit and reference flow, where applicable;
- data-quality controls;
- uncertainty and sensitivity treatment;
- confidence classification; and
- material evidence limitations.

## Effort and enabling requirements

Where possible, report:

- elapsed time;
- approximate practitioner effort;
- data acquisition effort;
- tooling requirements;
- skills or training required; and
- organizational dependencies.

## Outcomes

Describe the resulting:

- architectural decision or decision class;
- decision rationale;
- conditions or controls;
- changes to the original option;
- evidence improvements;
- lifecycle or circularity insights; and
- governance or assurance findings.

## Observed value

What did SDAF enable, improve or make visible that would otherwise have been difficult?

## Difficulties and deviations

Describe:

- requirements that were difficult to apply;
- unavailable evidence;
- adaptations made;
- unresolved ambiguity;
- disproportionate effort; and
- differences between the intended and actual process.

## Lessons for SDAF

Identify potential:

- clarifications;
- implementation guidance;
- templates;
- worked examples;
- interoperability requirements; or
- future normative changes.

## Limitations

Explain why the results should not be generalized beyond the stated scope.

## Supporting material

Link only to material that may be shared publicly and for which you have the necessary rights.

## Submission checks

- [ ] I have authority to share this information.
- [ ] Confidential, personal and security-sensitive information has been removed.
- [ ] Any adaptations or deviations from SDAF are clearly identified.
- [ ] The submission does not imply certification, endorsement or universal validation.
- [ ] Observations are distinguished from assumptions and interpretations.
